Spotting cheat-app (bot) drivers

Scope — HK truck · public-pool · 30d

More ▾

This page is about 38 cheat-app (bot) drivers. We looked at all public-pool truck drivers (van / mudou / mudou9; company orders left out), then kept the 38 who run a bot. Almost every order they released is On Demand (91% On Demand, 5% Same Day, 4% Next Day). Data pulled 2026-07-23, covering 30 days (24 Apr – 24 May 2026).

Driver Review Summary — 30d (24 Apr – 24 May 2026) — 4 flagged for manual review

More ▾

Who we can score fairly (active drivers)

  • What this means: not just logged in — they took enough trips that we can judge their behaviour
  • Rule: ≥30 orders taken (orders_assigned_30d), ≥30 finished (orders_completed_30d)
  • Period: 30d · 24 Apr – 24 May 2026

Top-tier review

  • 4 drivers were selected for manual review
  • Criteria: warning score ≥6 and at least one serious signal:
    • Customer churn
    • Higher-price same-driver loop

Most common serious pattern

↓

Important note

  • Not every flagged driver shows this loop.
  • A driver can be flagged because of any serious signal, not only the higher-price same-driver loop.
  • Bot speed (Step 1) is a separate check — not the same as this top-tier harm score.

Read left → right: everyone on the platform → drivers actually taking trips (not just online) → cheat-app bot speed → highest harm scores for a person to review.

How we count (read this once)

More ▾
Released vs cancelled — Released = driver took the order then released it (event_type_cd = 4, actor_type = 'Driver'). Cancelled = the order later ended with no driver (status = 'cancelled', cd 8 or 11) — used in section ⑥. Pool entry does not require a release (since 2026-07-27).
Who gets a score — mature cohort (T−90 to T−60): must took ≥30 orders (orders_assigned_30d), finished ≥30 (orders_completed_30d), not OA. If any rule fails → outside_analysis_pool (not scored yet; can still work).
Orders (booking-type mix on the top) — for the On Demand / Same Day / Next Day share only: each order counted once. That mix is not used in the +1 / +2 steps below.
Customer-churn steps (section ⑥) — bot pool only (38 drivers). We add up each driver’s counts from the mart (released_orders_90d → released_then_no_driver_90d → customer_no_return_60d_90d). Step 1 total = 19,249. If two bot drivers both released the same order, that order can appear twice in the sum — that is fine. All % in ⑥ use this same sum so they match BigQuery.

Bot spotting vs harm scoring — two separate checks

More ▾

Bot spotting ends at the bot pool (bar 3). The funnel answers “who is running a bot?” — 38 in the bot pool (1 at machine speed; see Step 1 above). ③ Harm tiers below then answers, within this bot pool only: “how much harm did each bot driver cause?” — a 0–8 score from churned customers, drivers cancelling a lot, and high assigned + release. Bot speed = detect the pool; the score = rank the damage inside it.

③ Harm tiers — warning score 0–8 → who to review (bot pool only) — who we score

More ▾

Bot spotting is done. From here we score the bot pool drivers in the 30d (24 Apr – 24 May 2026) — the rest are set aside. Each bot driver gets a warning score (0–8) and lands in a review band (review_priority). Higher score = more suspicious signs. Top band = score 6–8. How points are added → ④. Share % = among the bot pool.

⑥ Definition: "Customer churn" (+2) — what it means and how serious it is

How we define churn — forward 60 days + prior 90 days ≥1

More ▾

Churn definition: after the driver’s release, nobody else took the order and it cancelled — then that same customer places no new order for 60 days, and they had at least 1 order in the 90 days before → +2 (customer_no_return_60d_90d). Customers with 0 orders in the prior 90 days (new / dormant) are not counted and not scored. Numbers = bot pool only (38 drivers), mature cohort T−90 to T−60 (queried 2026-07-27).

Step by step (bot pool) Step 1 — driver released an order (event_type_cd = 4): 18,751 times.
Step 2 — nobody else took it → order cancelled: 1,362 (— of Step 1).
Step 3 — customer churn (forward 60 days + prior 90 days ≥1 order): 155 (— of Step 2) → +2 (customer_no_return_60d_90d).
Contrast (not scored): 175 had no new order within 30 days (customer_no_return_30d_90d).

Chart below: among scored churn only (forward 60 days and ≥1 order in the prior 90 days). Score is a flat +2. Prior-90 = 0 (new / dormant) is excluded — not shown, not counted.

The 155 churned customers — orders in their prior 90 days

scored churn only · prior 90 days ≥1 (churn_cust_recent_low/med/high_90d) · prior-90 = 0 excluded

Past 90 days (among scored churn)

Prior-90 = 0 is excluded. MEDIUM + HIGH = — had 3 or more orders in the 90 days before. Average among scored churn = ~1.73 orders in the prior 90 days.
Churn = forward 60 days with no new order, and prior 90 days ≥1. Total scored churn in this bot pool: 155.

⑦ Definition: driver cancels too many of their own orders (+3)

Rule (bot drivers only): driver cancel rate above bot-pool p75 → +3 (bad service).

Cut-off (bot-pool p75)

Bot-pool p75Score if
Cancels their own orders3.3%> 3.3%

How we count — why p75, field names

More ▾
Why the worst quarter (p75), not the average: a few drivers cancel a lot and drag the average up, so the average is unstable. The worst-quarter line barely moves when a few extreme drivers change.
Driver cancel = cancels by the driver themselves (event_type_cd = 3 AND actor_type = 'Driver'). Admin, system, and customer cancels are not counted.
Rate = driver cancels ÷ orders grabbed (driver_cancel_rate_30d). Above the bot-pool p75 (botpool_p75_driver_cancel_rate_30d, 3.3%) → +3 (driver_cancel_rate_above_botpool_p75_flag). Hits 8 / 38 bot drivers.

⑧ Definition: Bot score — assigned orders and order release rate both above bot median (+3)

Rule (bot drivers only): If assigned orders (30-day total) and order release rate are both higher than the typical bot driver (median) → +3.

Cut-offs (bot-pool median)

Bot medianScore if
Assigned orders (30-day total)136> 136
Order release rate19%> 19%

How we count — field names

More ▾
Assigned orders = orders_assigned_30d (count).
Order release rate = releases ÷ assigned (released_order_rate_30d).
Both above median → +3 (bot_assigned_and_release_above_bot_median_flag). Hits 11 / 38 bot drivers.
